condition.narrative: Grenada and OECS Commission:Pursuant to the Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.1(d), the Recipient shall develop andadopt a Project Operational Manual ("POM"), satisfactory to the Association, no later than thirty (30) days as of the EffectiveDate.

Grenada and Saint Lucia:Pursuant to the Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.C, the Recipient shall disclose and makeavailable to the public through official portals the statistics and Microdata, including census and survey reports and keydevelopment indicators, produced through the data collection operations conducted as part of the Project, in a manner consistentwith the POM, including (i) the Statistical Disclosure Calendar; and (ii) the applicable Personal Data protocols.

Grenada, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, and OECS Commission:The Recipient shall carry out the Project inaccordance with the Implementation Arrangements set out in Section I, Schedule 2 of the Financing Agreement.

OECS Commission:Pursuant to the Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.C.1, the Recipient shall develop a Sub-Grants Manual,in a manner and with contents acceptable to the Association, including, inter alia: (a) detailed arrangements and procedures inrelation to the Experiments, including the eligibility criteria, procedures, guidelines and templates for the selection, approval,administration and supervision of Experiments; (b) terms and conditions for the provision of Sub-Grants, including eligibilitycriteria, application, appraisal, approval and disbursement procedures; and; (c) an Implementation Agreement template.

Saint Lucia, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines: Pursuant to the Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.A.1(d), theRecipient shall develop and adopt a POM, satisfactory to the Association, no later than forty-five (45) days as of the EffectiveDate.

Saint Vincent and the Grenadines:Pursuant to the Financing Agreement, Schedule 2, Section I.C, the Recipient shall disclose andmake available to the public through official portals the statistics and Microdata, including census and survey reports and keydevelopment indicators, produced through the data collection operations conducted as part of the Project, in a manner consistentwith (a) the POM, including (i) the Statistical Disclosure Calendar; and (ii) the applicable Personal Data protocols; and (b) anyapplicable legislation; provided that in the event of any contradiction or inconsistency between (a) and (b) regarding PersonalData, the higher protection standard would apply.

title.narrative: Average number of household survey datasets per Participating Eastern Caribbean country accessible via the OECS Regional Microdata Catalog

comment.narrative:
Average number of household survey datasets per Participating Eastern Caribbean Country accessible via the OECS Regional Microdata Catalog. Datasets counted for this indicator are micro-/unit record data. FourÂ quarterly surveys (e.g. LFS) or a census sub-sample datasetÂ will be counted as 1 for this indicator.
To date, none of the participating countries has published micro datasets that would count towards this indicator. The Microdata Catalogue has been prepared by the OECS Commission and contains 13 microdatasets from the three Participating Countries. It has, however, not gone live yet. In addition, before microdatasets can be made accessible through the catalogue, development of data anonymization procedures and capacity as well as development of data privacy protocols and procedures are needed. Countries are just starting to work on these.

title.narrative: Customized Statistical Performance Indicator, average value for Participating Eastern Caribbean countries.
Customized Statistical Performance Indicator, average value for Participating Eastern Caribbean countries.

comment.narrative: To date, none of the participating countries has documented an improvement on the customized statistical performance indicator. In Saint Lucia, the country-level rating even fell, driven by a decline in the ODIN open data openness score compared to baseline and the legislation indicator becoming available but scoring 0. Revisions of Statistics Acts that are in progress or soon to start are expected to increase the indicator through the data infrastructure sub-component in Saint Lucia and SVG. With the delays in the SLCHBSs in all countries it is, however, unlikely that the overall target can be achieved before the closing of the Project. For this to happen, Saint Lucia and Grenada would need to conduct two rounds of the SLCHBS and have the data of the second round with the World Bank before June 2027 to produce comparable poverty headcounts at the International Poverty Line.
